thread.text:
Most arcade driving games give you a magical 'handbrake' button.

We built an endless EV drifting game where oversteer is initiated purely by weight transfer, throttle lift-off, and counter-steering.

Built entirely in raw Canvas with zero external libraries. 🧵👇
thread.mediaNote: High-framerate gameplay GIF showing a tight corner entry: trail-braking to shift weight forward, rear kicking out, and power-sliding past a roadside EV charger.

thread.text:
The driving physics breakdown:

• Weight transfer: Braking loads the front axle, freeing rear grip to pivot the car
• EV torque: Instant power delivery sustains the slip angle
• Regen dynamics: Off-throttle regen recharges the battery, while cutting off-road grass drains it 90x faster
thread.mediaNote: Side-by-side clip highlighting the Dual-View HUD (Cockpit glance + Top-Down tracker) with real-time kW draw and battery levels.

thread.text:
The technical stack is completely assetless:

🔊 Procedural WebAudio synth simulates dual-motor inverter whine (pitch mapped to wheel speed, amplitude to kW load, pitch-bent on regen)
🧪 Headless Chrome CDP automated suites verify slip angle physics invariants on every build
thread.mediaNote: Short video with sound demonstrating the dynamic WebAudio EV motor pitch rising on acceleration and dipping under regenerative braking.

thread.text:
Browser games lost their way when 60MB engine bundles and loading spinners took over.

Drift is a single, self-contained HTML file.

It loads in under 0.1 seconds, runs at locked 60 FPS on mobile and desktop, and has zero tracking, zero accounts, and zero pop-ups.
